 Judgment
Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, they are taken up for final disposal.

These appeals are filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge & MACT-VIII, Muddebhihal, in MVC Nos.663 & 664/2016 dated 05.09.2019.
02.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
03. The learned counsel for the petitioners in both cases submitted his argument that, the Tribunal has not passed the judgment and award in accordance with law and facts.
The Tribunal has awarded meager compensation.

Further he has submitted that after thorough investigation, the Investigating Officer has submitted charge-sheet against the driver of NEKRTC (for short 'Corporation'), but the Basappa @ Basavaraj S/O Amarappa ... vs The Managing Director on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166603586/

sentences.text: Tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record and come to the conclusion that there is contributory negligence on the part of PW.1 is 50% and contributory negligence on RW.1 is 50%.
On all these grounds, sought for allow the appeals.

04. As against this, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent/corporation has submitted his argument that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in para-15 to 17 of its judgment and has discussed the evidence in accordance with law and facts and come to the conclusion that there is contributory negligence on the part of PW.1 at 50%. That there are no grounds to interfere in this regard.
Further he has submitted that the Tribunal has passed the award in accordance with law and facts.

Further it is submitted that the appellants have not taken any grounds in the memorandum of appeal as to the contributory negligence of 50% on the rider of the motorcycle and 50% on the driver of the bus.
In the absence of grounds, this Court cannot interfere with the impugned judgment and award.
On all these grounds sought for dismissal of appeals.

05. Having heard arguments on both sides, the following points arise for consideration:
i) Whether the appellants in both cases have made out grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the contributory negligence and also regarding quantum of compensation?
ii) What order/award?
06.

My findings to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : Partly Affirmative Point No.2 : As per final order 07.

A perusal of the impugned judgment in para-15 to 17 the Tribunal has observed as under:
"15. RW.1 the driver of KSRTC bus has deposed that, he was driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA-33/F-0073.

He was proceeding from Talikoti towards Muddebihal, at about 6-45 pm when he reached near Kuntoji, motorcycle bearing No.KA.36/Q-1295 driven by PW-1 came from opposite side in rash and negligent manner and he took the bus to the side to avoid the accident.
Inspite of the same rider of the motorcycle came and hit the KSRTC bus.
The brother of PW-1 has lodged the complaint to Muddebihal police, which is a false complaint.
In the cross-examination, RW-1 admits that, he has been charge sheeted by the police.
However RW-1 states that, the accident did not occur due to his negligence.
The criminal case is pending against him.

Respondent has also examined the conductor of the said bus as RW-2, who has also deposed that, the accident occurred due to the negligence of PW-1, who has driven the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bus.
16. As seen from the spot mahazar Ex.P.5 the road at the spot runs East-West.
Talikoti is situated towards east and Muddebihal is situated towards west.

The bus Basappa @ Basavaraj S/O Amarappa ... vs The Managing Director on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166603586/
3 was coming from Talikoti towards Muddebihal.

sentences.text: The tar road has 18' width and on either side there is 5' mud road, the accident has occurred at a distance of 4 feet from the northern edge of the road towards south.
This would indicate that the bus was moving almost on the middle of the road.
If PW-1 had parked the motorcycle on the side of the road the bus would not have hit the motorcycle.
The motor vehicle accident report discloses that, no damages were found on the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA.33/F-0073.

Whereas, motorcycle bearing No.KA.36/Q-1295 has damages i.e., headlight assembly damaged, front indicators were damaged, speedometer unit damaged, front forks damaged, front registration number plate damaged and front wheel mudguard damaged.
The damages caused to the motorcycle would indicate that, the motorcycle has gone and hit the bus on the rear wheel.
I really bus has hit the motorcycle there would have bee some damages on the bus but absolutely no damages ar caused to the bus.
Further in the petitions the petitioner do not state that that bus hit the motorcycle.
It only stat that bus hit PW-1 and deceased Ningamma and they f along with the motorcycle, but, PW- 1 states that the bus the motorcycle and his wife died at the spot.

17. In the petition and evidence of PW-1 it is stated that, PW-1 stopped the vehicle by the side of the road, the bus came in a rash and negligent manner and has cut the vehicle in a curve shape and as a result rear wheel of the bus dashed to the motorcycle and Ningamma died at the spot and he sustained injuries.
As a result PW-1 fell on the road along with motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
If the motorcycle has fallen to the road, there would have been damages on the other parts of the motorcycle.
Whereas the Motor Vehicle Accident report discloses that, damages are only to the front portion of the motorcycle.
The spot sketch is not produced.
The Motor Vehicle Accident report as per Ex.P.6 creates doubt with regard to the rash and negligent driving of RW-1 in driving the KSRTC bus and causing the accident.
The accident spot shown in the mahazar and damages caused to the motorcycle coupled with evidence of PW-1 would clearly indicate that PW-1 is guilty of contributory negligence.

Therefore these issues are answered holding the PW-1 and RW-1 are equally liable for the cause of accident and the contributory negligence on the part of PW.1 is 50%
and contributory negligence on the part of RW.1 is 50%."

08. The oral and documentary evidence it is crystal clear that on the basis of the complaint filed by one Girimallappa, Muddebihal police have registered a case in Crime No.06/2016 against the driver of Corporation bus bearing Reg.No.KA-33/F-0073 for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304-A of IPC and submitted the FIR to the Court.

The inquest panchanama is also conducted by the Investigating Officer, in which also the Investigating Officer has answered question No.11 that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA-33/F-0073.
The police have rushed to the spot and conducted spot mahazar and obtained IMV report and wound certificate and recorded the statement of witnesses.

After thorough investigation, Investigating Officer has submitted the charge-sheet against the driver of the bearing Reg.No.KA-33/F-0073 for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 279,
337 and 304-A of IPC.

sentences.text: Though the charge-sheet is filed against the driver of the bus for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 304A of IPC.
The Tribunal has come to the conclusion that there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle on 50% and 50% on driver of bus.
The respondent has not challenged the charge-sheet submitted by the Investigating Officer before the concerned authority.

The Tribunal has observed in the impugned judgment that if PW.1 had parked motorcycle on the side of road, bus would not have hit motorcycle, but Investigating Officer has not stated in his charge-sheet that PW.1 has violated the Karnataka Traffic Act and Rules and also Regulations.
Without any accusation against the rider of the motorcycle the Tribunal has suo mutu discussed the fact that PW.1 had not parked the motorcycle on the side of the road, it cannot be accepted.
The Tribunal has not properly appreciated the evidence on record.
The Tribunal has ignored the documentary evidence placed by the claimants.

Therefore, in this regard,
considering the evidence placed by the claimants, I am of the considered view that the appellants have proved that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the bus bearing Reg.No.KA-33/F- 0073.
10.

Though the appellants have not stated in their memorandum of appeal as to the contributory negligence, in item-14 of the memorandum of appeal it is stated that the impugned judgment and award suffers from other infirmities.
Taking into consideration all these grounds the appeal cannot be rejected on the ground that the appellants have not specifically urged in the memorandum of appeal as to the contributory negligence.
Accordingly, respondent/corporation is liable to pay the compensation.

With regard to enhancement is concerned, MFA No.202217/2019 is arising out of MVC No.664/2016, the Tribunal in para-22 has observed as under:
"22.
Issue No.4 in MVC No.664/2016: Petitioner in MVC No.664/2016 has deposed that, he has sustained injuries in the accident.

In the petition he has states that, he had contusion at right parietal area, lacerated wound at right forearm below the right elbow, multiple abrasion at right all finger proximal, abrasion at right knee.
Ex.P7 is the wound certificate, which discloses that, petitioner has sustained four simple injuries.
Petitioner has not produced any medical bills.

Hence, petitioner is awarded for global compensation of Rs.10,000/- out of which respondent is liable to pay 50%
which amounts to Rs.5,000/-."
12. Considering the nature of injuries, it is just and proper to award global compensation in a sum of Rs.25,000/- as against Rs.5,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has taken notional income of the deceased at Rs.5,730/- per month instead of Rs.8,750/-.
The Tribunal has taken age of the deceased as 48 years as on the date of accident, then appropriate multiplier would be '13'.

As per decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.

Accordingly, point No.1 is answered partly in Affirmative.

ORDER
(i) MFA No.202217/2019 and MFA No.202218/2019 are allowed in part.

(ii) The Appellant/petitioner in MFA No.202217/2019 (MVC No.664/2016) is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.25,000/- as against Rs.5,000/- granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
